posts.title: A MacBook win, a surprise hug, and support for my dreams
posts.description: What winning a MacBook through Cardtonic Upskill 4.0 felt like, in a moment that took even me by surprise.
paragraphs: On Saturday, I broke character. I hugged a business acquaintance in broad daylight because Cardtonic had decided to support my dreams. He looked at me in surprise. I was showing a side of myself he had not seen before, and that was how happy I was.

I had won a MacBook through Upskill 4.0. Writing that down still feels special. The part I wanted to share first was not a specification or a photograph of a laptop. It was that unguarded reaction: excitement strong enough to interrupt the way I usually carry myself.

Cardtonic's first-checkpoint announcement had told applicants to check their inboxes for news of the next round. By October, I had my own news to share. My post on 11 October captured it better than a polished announcement could: Cardtonic had supported my dreams, and I could not hide how much that meant to me.

Cardtonic's first-review graphic reported 19,275 MacBook-track applications: 10,373 passed that review and 8,902 did not make it through. Those were early screening results, not the final winners. The programme offered 25 MacBooks, separately from its 20 tech scholarships. I eventually became one of the 25 MacBook winners.

Twenty-five winners out of 19,275 applications works out to one winner for every 771 applications, or about 0.13%. That is an overall selection ratio, not a calculation of my personal probability of winning. The scale of it helps explain why I was so excited: being one of those 25 meant a great deal to me.

My work brings together business analysis, executive support and digital systems, while I continue training in AI/ML engineering. That learning is still in progress. A win does not make the work finished or turn a developing skill into expertise. It is support for the work ahead, and I am grateful to have received it.
Thank you, Cardtonic, for this opportunity. I wanted my first post here to remember the feeling honestly: a Saturday, a surprised acquaintance, a spontaneous hug, and a very happy me.
